Address.description:
A position in a language's namespace: the package it belongs to and the
path within it — `fff :: [grep, types]` for a Rust module, path
components for a TypeScript file. Prefix relations, which are what a move
cares about, never hold across packages.

Answer.description:
The answer to a [`Request`]: the result type of the command asked. On
the wire it is that type's shape alone — a client knows what it asked —
so it serialises without a tag and is read back by the command's type.

Batch.description: `vvv batch`: several intents planned in sequence and applied as one.

files.description:
Every file any step touches, before the first step against after the
last. Edits are not listed per file: they belong to the steps, each in
the coordinates of the state before it.

BatchIntent.description:
Several intents planned in sequence, each against the state the previous
one leaves, and applied as one.

read_only.description: Whether this command is always read-only, including every supported option.

CaptureValue.description: `$A` binds one node; `$$$A` binds a sequence.

Confidence.description: How sure a rename is that an occurrence refers to its target declaration.

oneOf.description: Declared, imported, or reached by a path that resolves to the target.
A bare token with no evidence either way.
Resolves to a different declaration of the same name.

through.description:
The module it reaches the declaration through; the declaration's
own module at depth 1.

ContentId.description: Digest of the complete UTF-8 source text, independent of its path.

max_bytes.description: Maximum compact JSON bytes in the result, excluding the response envelope.

max_files.description: Maximum source files examined for incoming same-spelling references.

excerpt.description: Range of the returned text, which can be shorter than the target extent.

via.description: The exact occurrence establishing this relationship; absent for the seed.

enclosing.description: Location of the enclosing declaration, without repeating its body.

references_by_name.description: Incoming scanning covers this spelling only, not every possible alias.

ContinuationRecovery.description: A recovery action clients can branch on without parsing the error message.

Dead.description:
`dead [--lang]`: declarations nothing in the workspace refers to, with
how many tokens might.

DefinitionLocation.description: Enough information to select, open, or request context for a declaration.

source.description: Complete captured file. All spans remain absolute UTF-8 byte ranges.

Dep.description:
One import statement in the file and, when the layout can follow it,
where it leads.

address.description: What the path spells, as the layout places it.

alias.description:
The name the statement binds instead of the path's last segment:
`Cfg` in `use a::Config as Cfg`.

declares.description:
Part of an import statement (`use`, `import`), so it brings its last
segment into the file's scope. A qualified path in an expression
(`fff::GrepMatch` in a type position) is a reference to rewrite on a
move, but declares nothing.

file.description: The file declaring what the import reaches — the origin's when known.

glob.description: `use a::b::*`: every name under the path is brought into scope.

group.description:
Present when the path is an entry of a grouped import such as
`use a::{b, c::d}`; replacing `span` alone can then only express
paths that stay under the group's prefix.

origin.description:
The declaration the address reaches through re-exports, when that is
somewhere else: `vvv_core::text::span::Span` for `use vvv_core::Span`.

path.description:
The full path as written (`crate::a::b`, `../x/y`), parsed by the
grammar's [`PathSyntax`]. For a grouped entry this includes the
group's prefix.

reexport.description:
A `pub use`, an `export … from`: the name it brings in is offered on
again under this file's address, so a path to it here reaches the
original declaration.

start.description: Where the import starts, as a line and column.

Deps.description: `deps <path>`: what a file imports and who imports it.

module.description: The file's own module address, when the language has one.

Diff.description:
One file's change: the unified diff text (the wire) and its hunks (the
model).

ErrorCode.description: The kind of failure, stable across releases; the message is not.

oneOf.description: The caller cancelled the operation.
Resolution stopped before a complete answer was available.
The request could not be read: not JSON, or not a known command.
A query with none of pattern, kind, symbol, name.
A pattern or node kind the language's grammar rejects.
A selection naming rows or ids the search did not find.
A template naming a capture the match does not have.
No declaration by that name (and kind).
Several declarations share the name; `declared_in` picks one.
No registered language claims the file.
The language has no layout: paths cannot be followed, files not moved.
A position past the end of the file.
The destination already exists.
A file, or the file declaring a name, could not be found.
The layout refuses the move: a root, across packages, into itself.
Two edits of one plan overlap, or a file is moved twice.
A file changed since the plan (or the apply to undo) was made.
Nothing to undo, or a history file that cannot be read.
Reading or writing the tree failed.
Recovery could not restore or verify every attempted effect.

requested.description: Full extent being expanded; the excerpt is the returned subrange.

declared.description: Where that declaration's name starts, and the source line holding it.

import.description:
The import statement at the position, when it is inside one: what
it spells and where that really comes from.

importers.description:
Files whose imports resolve to the declaration, to any address a
re-export offers it at, or to its module when the declaration itself
is not addressable.

module.description: The file's module address, and the declaration's when a path reaches it.

symbol.description: The innermost declaration whose extent contains the position.

via.description: Every other address a re-export chain offers the declaration at.

Exposed.description: A declaration as the graph holds it: placed, with its reach.

extent.description:
The declaration with what belongs to it in the text: leading
attributes and doc comments, an enclosing `export`. What moving the
declaration cuts; what an outline shows.

importers.description: Files in the workspace importing it, at any of its addresses.

name_span.description: The identifier token itself: what a rename replaces.

start.description: Where the declaration's name starts, as a line and column.

via.description: The other addresses it is offered at, through re-exports.

visibility.description:
The visibility as written (`pub(crate)`, `export`); `None` when the
declaration has no modifier. What it means is the language's
[`Semantics`](crate::Semantics).

Failure.description: A failed request, as the wire carries it.

hint.description: What to try instead, when there is something.

recovery.description: Effects that could not be restored after a failed mutation.

File.description: One file as it is, with syntax colouring and declaration ranges.

identifiers.description: Versioned identifier occurrences from this exact source.

symbols.description: Declarations from the same source snapshot as the text and highlights.

FileChange.description: One file a plan touches: its edits and the whole-file diff.

moved_to.description: Path after, when the file is moved.

HighlightKind.description:
The classes a display distinguishes. Coarse on purpose: enough to read
code, not enough to argue about.

entries.description: Oldest first; the last entry is what `vvv undo` would reverse.

HistoryEntry.description: One apply that can still be undone.

intent.description: What was applied, as data; the display layer renders it.

moves.description: Moves it made, as (from, to) pairs: what undo reverts.

paths.description: The files it wrote, at their pre-apply paths: what undo restores.

Impact.description:
`impact <name>`: every module that would feel a change to a declaration —
those importing it, then those importing them, outward.

consumers.description: Nearest first: depth 1 imports the declaration itself.

ImportGroup.description:
Where a grouped entry sits, so a surgery can rewrite it in place or move
it out of the group.

item.description: The whole entry, alias or nested list included (`parse::Config as Cfg`).

items.description: How many entries that list has.

list.description: The innermost list the entry belongs to, braces included.

prefix.description: Combined prefix of the enclosing groups (`crate::util`).

top_level.description: Whether `list` is the statement's own list rather than a nested one.

ImportSite.description: One path in one file. `span` covers exactly the text a rewrite replaces.

The name the statement binds instead of the path's last segment:

ImportsReport.description:
`imports [path]`: import statements worth a look — unused, unresolved,
or the same target twice.

path.description: The file asked about; every file when absent.

redundant.description:
Declared imports naming an address another statement in the file
already brings in.

unplaced.description:
Files whose language has a layout but which it cannot place — a
crate's integration tests, say — so their imports were not judged.

unresolved.description: Declared imports the layout could not place.

unused.description: Declared imports whose bound name the file never spells again.

Intent.description:
Any mutating request, as one value: what history records, what a summary
renders, what a remote client sends.

oneOf.description:
Several intents planned in sequence, each against the state the
previous one leaves, and applied as one.

Locations.description: `where <name>`: where `name` is declared and how to reach each site.

address.description:
For a declaration in an addressable file: its module address, the
value `outline` gives it. Filled by the engine, which has the project.

content.description: Complete source version; absent only in older serialized matches.

line.description: The source line on which the match starts, for display in context.

MatchId.description:
Content-derived identifier: the same file, range and text yield the same id
across runs, so a selection made from one `search` can drive a later command.

Modifier.description: A visibility modifier as it appears in the source.

ModulePath.description:
A path as spelled in source: its head and its segments, with the syntax
that spells it. Serialises as the text, so the wire is what the user
wrote.

Move.description: `vvv move`: a file or directory moved, its importers respelled.

from_address.description: The module address before and after, when the language has one.

notices.description: References vvv found but could not rewrite.

respellings.description:
References rewritten in place; every other edit in `files` is
structural (a `mod` line moved, a visibility widened).

MoveIntent.description: Move a file and make every reference to it follow.

MoveSymbol.description: `vvv move --symbol`: one declaration moved between files.

from.description: The declaration's address before and after.

respellings.description:
Consumers rewritten in place; every other edit in `files` is the
declaration itself moving.

MoveSymbolIntent.description:
Move one declaration — with what belongs to it in the text, and for Rust
its `impl` blocks — from the file declaring it to another file of the
same language, and make every reference follow.

to.description: The file to declare it in; it must exist.

Name.description: One identifier: a module, a declaration, a file stem. Compared by text.

Notice.description:
Something a plan could not do and a human should look at. Never fatal:
the rest of the plan is still valid. Data only; the display layer words it.

oneOf.description:
An import the layout understood but the surgery could not rewrite in place;
`replacement` is what it should become.

After the move, `from` references `item` but may not see it, and the
widening it would take is not one vvv makes on its own (making a
declaration public across packages is the author's call).

An import that now names a declaration in its own file, inside a
grouped statement vvv does not split for this; remove the entry.

Occurrence.description: A token spelling the renamed name, with what the imports could tell.

address.description:
For a declaration in an addressable file: its module address, the
value `outline` gives it. Filled by the engine, which has the project.

content.description: Complete source version; absent only in older serialized matches.

line.description: The source line on which the match starts, for display in context.

Outline.description: `outline <path>`: what a file declares, in order.

module.description: The file's own module address, when the language has one.

OutlineItem.description: A declaration found in one file.

address.description:
The module address the declaration is reached by, when a path can
reach it in this language.

extent.description:
The declaration with what belongs to it in the text: leading
attributes and doc comments, an enclosing `export`. What moving the
declaration cuts; what an outline shows.

name_span.description: The identifier token itself: what a rename replaces.

reach.description: Who may name it, from its modifier and its module.

start.description: Where the extent starts and ends, as lines and columns.

visibility.description:
The visibility as written (`pub(crate)`, `export`); `None` when the
declaration has no modifier. What it means is the language's
[`Semantics`](crate::Semantics).

PackageId.description:
The name a package goes by in paths: a Rust crate's lib name (`fff`, not
`fff-search`), a TypeScript package's name. The layout decides the spelling.

excerpt.description: Range of the returned text, which can be shorter than the target extent.

via.description: The exact occurrence establishing this relationship; absent for the seed.

Position.description:
Zero-based line and character column. Columns count `char`s, not bytes,
so they are safe to show to humans and editors.

language.description: Restrict to one language; otherwise every registered language is searched.

name.description: Only declarations with exactly this name.

pattern.description: ast-grep style pattern with meta-variables, e.g. `fn $NAME($$$ARGS) { $$$ }`.

Reach.description:
The set of modules that may name a declaration: a kind applied to the
declaring module's address. Never declared, always computed.

ReachKind.description: What a visibility modifier means, relative to the declaring module.

oneOf.description: The declaring module and its descendants (Rust private).
The parent module and its descendants (`pub(super)`).
The whole package (`pub(crate)`).
Everyone (`pub`, `export`).
A module named in the modifier (`pub(in a::b)`); the layout resolves it.

Reason.description:
What the file's imports and paths said about an occurrence: the ground
for its [`Confidence`]. Views tag `?` and `✗` sections with it.

oneOf.description: Written in the module that declares the target.
An import resolving to the target brings the name in.
The tail of a qualified path resolving to the target.
A glob (or whole-file) import opens the declaring module.

Reached through a re-export (`use vvv_core::Span` for
`vvv_core::text::span::Span`) that vvv followed to the declaration.

Syntax could not place it; an oracle — a build, a language server —
said it is the declaration.
A bare name nothing imports, or a path whose head cannot be placed.

No declaration to judge against: a method or field, reached through
a type; the token merely spells the name.
Resolves to another declaration of the same name in the workspace.
Resolves into a package outside the workspace.
Syntax could not place it; an oracle said it is another declaration.

Recovery.description: A recovery result; unknown states are separate from confirmed residual effects.

References.description:
`references <name>`: the declarations called `name` and every token that
spells it, each judged against the declaration meant.

RelPath.description:
A file's path inside the workspace, spelled the way the project does: `/`
on every platform.

A workspace path is a project path — like a `mod` path or a
`crate::a::b` address — not a path of the machine, so it carries its own
spelling and is what goes on the wire, into a row, or into a diagnostic.
It reads as a [`Path`] (an OS path is made from one at the edge, where a
file is actually read), but it cannot spell a separator the host's way:
`Display`, serde and the stored bytes are always `/`.

oneOf.description: A call to a local/parameter/value binding does not identify the invoked function.

call.description: None denotes a non-call reference, including imports and value references.

caller.description: Owner of a call site; absent for non-call references and anonymous callables.

site.description: Exact identifier (or unsupported callee expression) providing the evidence.

limitations.description: Known gaps remain even when the candidate scan finishes.

scan_complete.description: Completion of the candidate scan, not proof of a complete runtime call graph.

unresolved_imports.description: Import bindings that could not be resolved while discovering alias spellings.

unsupported_files.description: Files whose plugin does not provide syntactic call facts.

Rename.description: `vvv rename`: the declaration and every occurrence, each judged.

declarations.description: Where `name` is declared; more than one means the rename is ambiguous.

occurrences.description:
Every identifier spelling the name, each judged against the target;
their ids feed a later `--select`.

RenameIntent.description:
Rename the declaration(s) called `name` and every identifier that spells it.

Resolution is syntactic: every occurrence of the identifier in files of
the declaring language is an occurrence. The `selection` is how a human or
agent excludes the ones that are not the same symbol.

declared_in.description: The file declaring the symbol meant, when several share the name.

addresses.description: The binding's address followed by each re-export address, in order.

oneOf.description: Enough information to select, open, or request context for a declaration.
Enough information to select, open, or request context for a declaration.

Respelling.description:
A reference a move re-spelled in place: where it is, what it said and
what it says now. A preview lists these as one row each instead of a
diff hunk; an edit no respelling accounts for is structural and shows as
a hunk.

span.description: The reference's span before the move — the edit that rewrites it.

Rewrite.description: `vvv rewrite`: one edit per selected match.

RewriteIntent.description: Replace every selected match of `query` with `template`.

Role.description:
What position a match occupies in its file: the declaration itself, a
token inside an import statement, or any other use. Views lead with
declarations and dim imports; the engine orders results by it.

SchemaDocument.description: A Draft 2020-12 schema, including all definitions needed to use it offline.

SchemaReferences.description: Identifiers of bundled, locally retrievable command contracts.

Search.description: `vvv search`: what was found, and which languages could not be asked.

skipped.description:
Languages whose grammar could not compile the query; their files
were not searched.

address.description:
For a declaration in an addressable file: its module address, the
value `outline` gives it. Filled by the engine, which has the project.

content.description: Complete source version; absent only in older serialized matches.

line.description: The source line on which the match starts, for display in context.

ordinal.description: Absolute, one-based position in the complete search ordering.

SearchScope.description:
Explicit file/directory prefixes and owning package names or IDs.
Alternatives within each list are ORed; the two lists are intersected.

Selection.description:
Which matches of a search a later command acts on.

Ids are content-derived, so a selection made from `vvv search` can be
handed to `vvv rewrite` in a separate process. Ordinals are the 1-based
positions in the same search's result order, which is what human output
numbers rows with. Either kind that no longer resolves means the files
changed in between; the selection is then refused rather than silently
narrowed.

import.description:
The import statement that brings it into the file asked from, spelled
as that language writes it.

Skipped.description:
A language a search left out, and why: its grammar could not compile the
query (a Rust pattern on a TypeScript tree). Never fatal; the other
languages' matches are complete. Data only; the display layer words it.

SnapshotId.description: Opaque identity of captured source and project inputs; not a disk transaction.

Span.description: Half-open byte range `[start, end)` inside a single file.

Surface.description: `surface [package]`: what a package offers to everyone, and who takes it.

package.description: The package asked about; every package when absent.

SymbolKind.description: What a declaration declares, in vocabulary shared by every language.

oneOf.description:
An `impl` block, named after the type it is for. Not a declaration a

SymbolRef.description: A declaration in one source version, not an identity across edits.

restored.description: Files restored to their pre-apply contents, at their pre-apply paths.

unsure.description:
